public import FormalConjecturesUtil

/-!
# Class number problem for real quadratic fields

*Reference:* [Wikipedia](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Class_number_problem)
-/

@[expose] public section

open Polynomial
namespace ClassNumberProblem

def IsClassNumberOne (d : ℤ) : Prop :=
  ∃ (h₂ : Irreducible (X ^ 2 - C (d : ℚ))),
  have := Fact.mk h₂
  NumberField.classNumber (AdjoinRoot (X ^ 2 - C (d : ℚ))) = 1

/--
There are infinitely many real quadratic fields `ℚ(√d)` with class number one,
where `d > 1` is a squarefree integer.
-/
@[category research open, AMS 11]
theorem class_number_problem :
    { d : ℤ | Squarefree d ∧ d > 1 ∧ IsClassNumberOne d }.Infinite := by
  sorry

/--
**Stark–Heegner theorem** : For any squarefree integer `d < 0`, the class number of the imaginary
quadratic field Q(√d) is one if and only if `d ∈ {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163}`.
-/
@[category research solved, AMS 11]
theorem class_number_problem.variants.imaginary :
    { d : ℤ | Squarefree d ∧ d < 0 ∧ IsClassNumberOne d } =
    {-1, -2, -3, -7, -11, -19, -43, -67, -163} := by
  sorry

end ClassNumberProblem

reformulations.difference: Lean asserts infinitude of squarefree integer radicands d > 1, rather than directly asserting infinitude of real quadratic fields.
reformulations.equivalence_argument: Every real quadratic field is isomorphic to ℚ(√d) for a unique squarefree integer d > 1. Conversely, every such d defines a real quadratic field. AdjoinRoot (X² − C d) constructs that field, and class number is invariant under field isomorphism. Thus these radicands bijectively parametrize the relevant isomorphism classes, preserving the class-number-one condition and infinitude.

review.notes: Checked the definition and both theorems. NumberField.classNumber uses the ordinary ideal class group of the full ring of integers, not merely ℤ[√d]. The imaginary variant exactly matches the source's radicand list. Wikipedia still records real-field infinitude as open and the imaginary classification as solved. Checks in /workspace/review/scratch.lean compile successfully: irreducibility is equivalent to the radicand being nonsquare and follows from the stated restrictions; the existential proof witness does not alter the predicate; the quotient has degree two and the expected root relation; square radicands are rejected; and all nine listed integers satisfy the squarefree/sign filters. No problem theorem was used to establish these checks.
